3. Facts leading to the disposal of the revision is that the suit land measuring an area of 9.52 acres appertaining to R.S. Khatian No.150 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No.140 of Mouza North Gabtala, Police Station-Pirojpur originally belonged to Chandra Kanta Mridha and Kali Kumar Maridha in equal share; Kali Kumar Mridha separated his 8 annas share and new Khatian No.191 was opened in his name; that Kali Kumar Mridha had no son, but he had 4 daughters, namely Kanchan Bala, Tagar Bala, Jasoda and the plaintiff Kiran Bala; that Kanchan Bala was married to Kali Kumar alias Satish Chandra Mondol of Alamkathi; that Kanchan Bala left for India after 4/5 years and she had been living with her husband at Bagjola Camp in India; Tagar Bala and Jasoda died during life time of their father; that Kanchan Bala died on 20' Poush, 1378 B.S. at Bagjola Camp in India during the life time of her father; Kali Kumar and as such she did not inherit her father's property; that Kanchan Bala had a son namely Jatindra Nath, who died after 2 years of the death of his mother; that the plaintiff-Kiran Bala was married to Anil Chandra Bairagi of village-Dakatia and she had been living with her husband; that the plaintiff's mother died while the plaintiff was minor and thereafter plaintiff's father brought a woman to bring up the plaintiff and after the marriage of the plaintiff the said woman died; that thereafter the plaintiffs father brought another woman namely. Malati Rani on condition to give her one bigha of land and accordingly the plaintiff's father executed and registered a Kol-Karsha Patty in respect of .68 decimals of land on 05.01.1953 in favour of Malati Rani who has been possessing the same; that after the death of Kanchan Bala the plaintiff's father fell ill and at the request the plaintiff went to her fathers house in the month of Baisakh, 1379 B.S. and since then she had been living there; that in the month of Chaitra, 1382 B.S. the physical condition of the plaintiffs father was seriously worsen and as such the plaintiff's husband and son went to the plaintiff's house in the month of Baisakh and since then they have been living there permanently; that thereafter the plaintiff's father died in the month of Ashar, 1383 B.S. and as such the property left by Kali Kumar devolved upon the plaintiff; that the plaintiff transferred one Bigha of land to Ananta. Nakul and Billabasini by registered kabala; that the defendant Nos.1 and 2 having had the prior knowledge that Kanchan Bala died in India and that the plaintiff has been owning and possessing the suit land after the death of her father managed to mutate the name of Kanchan Bala and the plaintiff in the respective khatian by Mutation Case No.112/P/IX (1)/177-78 that the neither the plaintiff nor her sister Kanchan Bala filed the said Mutation Case nor they put their signature of L.T.I. in the petition for mutation; that the defendant Nos. l and 2 have falsely mutated the names of the plaintiff and Kanchan Bala in collusion with the defendant No.4 who is a local U.P. : Member; that the defendant Nos.1 and 2 obtained false succession certificate through defendant No.4 and procured false report from the Tahsilder that the defendants Nos.l-3 threatened the plaintiff to dispossess her from the suit land in the month of Baisakh, 1387 B.S. stating that they have obtained kabalas from Kanchan Bala; the plaintiffs obtained certified copies of the said three kabalas on 06.11.1978; that the plaintiff requested the defendant Nos.I-3 to execute a deed of relinquishment but they refused on 151h Jaistha, 1389 B.S. in favour of the plaintiff and hence the suit. 

 4. Defendant Nos. l and 2 contested the suit by filing joint written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contending inter alia, that the suit khatin land belonged to two full brothers Chandra Kumar and Kali Kumar in equal share; that Chandra Kumar died leaving two sons, defendant Nos. l and 2; that Kali Kumar died leaving two daughters Kanchan Bala and Kiran Bala to inherit his share; that Kanchan Bala and Kiran Bala mutated their names in the respective khatian vide order dated 17.05.1978 in Mutation Case No. 1 12 /P/IX(Iy177-78; that Kanchan Bala transferred 1.70 acres of land in favour of defendant Nos.1 and 2 by two registered kabalas dated (95 Kartik, 1385 B.S. on consideration of Take 16,000.00 and delivered possession thereof; that the defendant Nos. l and 2 mutated their names and by paying rents to the government; that the plaintiff was well aware of the said kabalas. It further stated that the plaintiff filed a petition before Martial Law authority and officer-in-charge of the local police station made enquiry and submitted report contending that the allegation is false; that Kanchan Bala performed the 'Sradha' of her father with the consideration money: that Kanchan Bala is still alive and left from India in 1387 B.S.; that Kanchan Bala has a son named Jatindra who is still alive in India; that the defendant Nos. l and 2 has been possessing the suit land since their purchase. With these averments defendant prayed for dismissal of the suit.
